sentences.text: Wumengosaurus was a small aquatic reptile that lived during the Middle Triassic in Guizhou, southwestern China. Its total body length ranged from 95.5 to 130.5 centimeters.
The genus was first described by Jiang and colleagues in 2008.
The type species of the genus is Wumengosaurus delicatomandibularis, which is the species the genus is based on.
A second species, Wumengosaurus rotundicarpus, was described by Qin and colleagues in 2021.
Wumengosaurus was originally classified as a basal eosauropterygian, but in 2023, Xu and colleagues reclassified it as a derived pachypleurosaurid.
Recent analyses place Wumengosaurus as the sister taxon to the clade containing Luopingosaurus and Honghesaurus.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Wumengosaurus as Eosauropterygia, and the animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
One phylogenetic analysis suggested Wumengosaurus is the sister taxon to Ichthyosauromorpha, though this was not formally repositioned in the classification.
